# color-spaces.types: ColorLCh

```plato

// CIELAB in cylindrical form: lightness, chroma (colorfulness), and hue angle.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HCL_color_space)
type ColorLCh
    implements IValue
{
    L: Number;
    Chroma: Number;
    Hue: Angle;
}

// A color in CIELUV: an alternative perceptual space favored for additive
// (emissive) displays. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIELUV)
type ColorLuv
    implements IValue
{
    L: Number;
    U: Number;
    V: Number;
}

// A color in OkLab: a modern perceptual space with better hue linearity than
// CIELAB; the preferred space for perceptual blending and gradients.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklab_color_space)
type ColorOkLab
    implements IValue
{
    L: Number;
    A: Number;
    B: Number;
}

// OkLab in cylindrical form: lightness, chroma, and hue angle.
type ColorOkLCh
    implements IValue
{
    L: Number;
    Chroma: Number;
    Hue: Angle;
}

//==
// # Palettes, harmony, and color difference
//
// Colors considered as a set rather than one at a time: an ordered palette (a
// swatch list, an indexed-image color table, a categorical scale), the
// hue-wheel relationships used to derive one from a base color, and the delta
// E formulas that measure how far apart two colors look.

//==
// ## Palettes, harmony, and difference

// An ordered set of colors used together: a swatch list, an indexed-image
// color table, or a categorical scale.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palette_(computing))
type Palette
    implements IValue
{
    Colors: Array<Color>;
}

// A classical hue-wheel relationship used to derive palettes from a base color.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony_(color))
type ColorHarmony
    = Complementary
    | Analogous
    | Triadic
    | SplitComplementary
    | Tetradic
    | Square
    | Monochromatic;

// A perceptual color-difference (delta E) formula.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_difference)
type ColorDifference = CIE76 | CIE94 | CIEDE2000 | CMC | EuclideanOkLab;

//==
// # Device-referred and video color models
//
// Colors expressed the way a device, codec, or press expects them: gamma-
// encoded sRGB, the luma-plus-chroma video forms, subtractive CMYK ink
// coverage, the CSS hue/whiteness/blackness model, and sampled spectra. These
// are interchange forms — decode to the linear-light `Color` (`color.types.plato`)
// before doing arithmetic on them.

//==
// ## Device-referred and video color types

// A gamma-encoded sRGB color with alpha, components nominally in [0, 1]: the
// interchange form of most 2D content. Decode to linear `Color` before
// arithmetic. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRGB)
type ColorSRGB
    implements IValue
{
    R: Number;
    G: Number;
    B: Number;
    A: Number;
}

// A color as luma Y plus U/V chroma differences (analog video convention).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y%E2%80%B2UV)
type ColorYUV
    implements IValue
{
    Y: Number;
    U: Number;
    V: Number;
}

// A color as luma Y plus Cb/Cr chroma offsets (digital video and JPEG
// convention). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YCbCr)
type ColorYCbCr
    implements IValue
{
    Y: Number;
    Cb: Number;
    Cr: Number;
}

// A subtractive process color: cyan, magenta, yellow, and key (black) ink
// coverages, each in [0, 1]. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMYK_color_model)
type ColorCMYK
    implements IValue
{
    Cyan: Number;
    Magenta: Number;
    Yellow: Number;
    Key: Number;
}

// A color as a hue angle plus whiteness and blackness mixed in (the CSS HWB
// model); an intuitive tint/shade parameterization.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HWB_color_model)
type ColorHWB
    implements IValue
{
    Hue: Angle;
    Whiteness: Number;
    Blackness: Number;
}

// A color as a sampled spectral power distribution. Wavelengths ascend and
// pair one-to-one with Amplitudes (relative power per sample).
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectral_power_distribution)
type SpectralColor
    implements IValue
{
    Wavelengths: Array<Length>;
    Amplitudes: Array<Number>;
}
```
